title: How to get paid to clip streamers: campaigns, rights and workflow
description: Learn how clipper campaigns pay, what permission and payout rules to check, and how to edit an authorized Twitch or Kick clip on iPhone.
primaryKeyword: how to get paid to clip streamers

blocks.html: People who clip streamers can earn from a streamer- or brand-funded campaign, a direct editing job, or their own eligible channel monetization. Those are different deals. A campaign may pay per approved post, per verified view, or for a fixed deliverable; a platform may reject a reposted clip even when the streamer gave permission. Read the terms before you edit, and get written permission for the exact source and use.

This paid workflow is part of the wider clip economy, where creators hire people to turn long streams and shows into short posts. The Atlantic’s 2026 discussion of clipping describes that shift; it does not promise that any particular clip or campaign will earn money. Read the reporting on the clip economy.

blocks.html: Choose a way to get paid

• Join a funded clipping campaign. The campaign owner supplies the brief and footage or confirms what you may use. Payment can be per approved post, per 1,000 verified views, or a fixed retainer. For example, the current Content Rewards creator terms describe CPM, per-post, retainer and pool campaigns. Terms differ by campaign, so check the page you are joining.
  • Work for a streamer or editor directly. Agree on a fee, number of clips, deadlines, review rounds, platforms and rights in writing. A fixed fee pays for agreed editing work; a performance bonus depends on the contract.
  • Build a channel that qualifies for platform revenue.YouTube reviews a channel’s overall originality. Its reused-content policy can reject minimally changed clips even when the original creator gave permission. TikTok’s Creator Rewards guidance says eligible videos must be original, high-quality and longer than one minute, with access and eligibility depending on the account and market. A short repost does not qualify just because it gets views.

Some KICK Bounties are open to viewers, and some let viewers submit a clip as an entry. KICK lists rewards such as gifted subscriptions or KICK Shop gift cards. Its separate streamer-focused Bounties describe KICK or brand partners paying streamers for clips. Read the viewer guide and streamer payout details. Eligibility and rewards vary by Bounty, and a viewer prize is not necessarily cash, so check the specific terms before counting it as paid clipper work.

blocks.html: Check the brief before you make a clip

A public stream or a working clip button is not permission to repost the video elsewhere. Twitch lets broadcasters control whether viewers can make clips, and KICK explains how viewers can create and download its clips. Those tools describe platform actions; they do not promise that the streamer has licensed off-platform edits or paid promotion. Ask the streamer or campaign owner to confirm the rights in writing. Twitch clip settings and KICK clip creation and downloads are useful for understanding the source platform.

• Which recording, channel and timestamps may you use?
  • Which accounts and platforms may you post to, and for how long?
  • May you crop, caption, translate, add voice-over or change the audio?
  • What counts as an approved post and a verified view?
  • Is there a minimum, a maximum payout, a review window or a fee?
  • What disclosure, credit and post-submission rules apply?

Check the source audio too. A streamer may be allowed to play music during a live broadcast without owning rights to put that music in a clip on another service. Get permission for the whole edit, including music, overlays and guest appearances. If a paid post endorses a product, use the platform’s branded-content tools and check local disclosure rules. For U.S. posts, check the FTC’s guidance and make the financial relationship clear to viewers.

blocks.html: Edit a permitted stream file on iPhone

• Start with a file the creator or campaign has authorized. For a KICK clip, the help center says its Download button saves an MP4. Move that file to iPhone Photos or Files. For Twitch, request the approved source file or use a sharing method the campaign permits.
  • Import the file from Photos or Files in ReelClip. The app edits recordings already on your iPhone; it does not capture or download a Twitch or KICK stream.
  • Choose Slice when you have one moment and want to set its start and end. Choose Cut when you want to divide a longer authorized recording by clip count, duration and spacing. The app does not decide which moments are funny or likely to perform.
  • For speech, use Transcript to find a passage, then check names and play the full thought in context. Review the framing separately: selecting a shorter time range does not turn a landscape picture into a vertical crop.
  • Open Review, watch each prepared clip and export the ones the brief allows. Export requires Creator. Upload the saved file yourself, then submit its link and track the campaign’s stated measurement window.

ReelClip prepares clips; it does not publish them to social platforms, grant rights to someone else’s footage or guarantee campaign approval or earnings. See the existing guide to Cut and the guide to Transcript for the actual editing controls.
